newsitem.title: GERMANY: German Jan insolvencies rise 5.9 pct - Stats Office.
newsitem.headline: German Jan insolvencies rise 5.9 pct - Stats Office.

text.p: The number of German insolvencies in January rose 5.9 percent year-on-year, although the increase does not indicate a weakening in the economy, the Federal Statistics Office said on Thursday.
After moderate declines in November and December last year, insolvencies in January rose to 2,482, including a 7.3 percent climb in company bankruptcies to 2,004.
But the Statistics Office said the January figures rose against unusually low totals from January 1996.

"This increase at the beginning of the year does not signal a further increase in the next months," the office said in a statement. "Much more it points to the fact that for January 1996 extraordinarily few insolvencies were reported, in comparison to the rest of the months of 1996."

Total west German insolovencies rose 6.5 percent to 1,808 for January, while bankruptcy claims by companies increased 8.3 percent to 1,416. In eastern Germany, the total rose 4.3 percent to 674, and company insolvencies increased five percent to 588.
